title: One Flowchart for Every Animal Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A sponge, a jellyfish, an earthworm and a crow. Chapter 4 gives us eleven phyla and then the classes of vertebrates: too many to remember one by one. Aarav likes machines, so he asks: can one flowchart sort every animal with a few yes or no questions?

We build the whole key from the basis of classification in NCERT, branch by branch, as a living diagram: level of organisation (Porifera), symmetry and germ layers (Coelenterata, Ctenophora), the body cavity (Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, the coelomates) and the notochord (Chordata, then jaws, fins or limbs down to the classes). Then we run it: an earthworm and a crow travel down the key and land on Annelida and Aves. A jellyfish vs starfish comparison, a pause and think check on the leech, a worked example (Sycon, Taenia, Ascaris, Columba), the exam trap about echinoderms, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 39 of our PUC Biology series, and it completes Part 1: Diversity in the Living World.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Too many animals to remember
0:34 The four questions of the key
0:53 Build the key, branch by branch
1:50 Run the key: an earthworm and a crow
2:12 Jellyfish vs starfish + pause and think
3:01 Worked example: four animals down the key
3:28 Exam trap: where do echinoderms go?
3:49 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:20 Recap and three questions to answer

Part 1 complete: all four chapters of Diversity in the Living World are done. Find every episode in the PUC Biology playlist.
